review_basis: Enumerated committed and working-tree changes against main and compared them with the task allowlist; zero unexpected files were present.
Inspected the complete product diff for overflow measurement, viewport bounds, minimap projection, tag editing and context-menu removal.
Confirmed the text renderer no longer collapses the textarea to 0px and the sizing policy returns the current height when content fits.
Confirmed React Flow, footer input, viewport state publication/animation and document normalization all enforce the 0.1% to 100% range.
Confirmed visible layer-order labels and updateSelectedNodeLayer are absent while duplicate and delete actions remain.
Re-ran all 301 Canvas tests, TypeScript and production build after the audit.
non_blocking_findings: At 0.1% zoom, extremely large canvas extents remain possible by design; visual-scale compensation is capped at 10 to avoid oversized borders and handles.
The production build succeeded using the locked local Next.js and TypeScript binaries because the pnpm wrapper stopped at its dependency build-approval policy before starting the requested scripts.
Manual pointer/UI acceptance is still recommended for wheel zoom, long wrapped text, minimap centering and tag-marker readability.
suggested_tests: Create a large text node, type content that fits, then cross the lower boundary and confirm a single monotonic vertical growth step.
Zoom from 100% down to 0.1% with the wheel and footer slider, then use 回到中心.
Assign several tags to nodes and confirm minimap colors appear at matching spatial positions.
risk_notes: Internal zIndex persistence and export compatibility remain intact; only user-facing reorder actions were removed.
Legacy imageTags remain readable by the minimap color projection.
